brief: Build an unrelated trail-checkpoint admission queue, not a search or citation feature. The executable reads records only from standard input. Its literal separator is ';', numeric rejection-report cap is 2, and assigned ordering is ordinal identifier ascending. These are fixed candidate constants rather than runtime choices. The public requirements fully define identifiers, priority syntax, newline rules, rejection, the assigned sort algorithm, capping, and six-line output; no arguments or external files are used.
publicExamples: For separator ';', BAY_2;0005 is lexically valid; bay;5, BAY;+5, and BAY; 5 are rejected.
Duplicate accepted identifiers remain duplicate entries in `ids=`; identifiers cannot contain commas, so no escaping is needed.
The rationale is part of the submission, but the public prompt intentionally does not supply its trace or mutation evidence.
rationalePrompt: Trace one representative input through your typed model, explain how you decomposed the foreign contract into records and methods, and identify the observable result that would expose a deficient implementation.

requirements.text: Build Verisearch.slnx on .NET 10 with nullable analysis and warnings-as-errors enabled.

Create the sealed positional records `RankedEntry(string Id, int Priority)` and `RankingResult(IReadOnlyList<string> Ids, int Accepted, int Rejected)`. Inside RankingContract, implement `RankedEntry? Parse(string line, char separator)` and `RankingResult Rank(string input, char separator, string failureMode, string outputOrder)`. Rank must call Parse for each retained segment and return the RankingResult that the top-level program writes; dummy members plus a separate inline implementation do not satisfy this public structure contract.

The evaluator supplies at most 10,000 LF-delimited segments that are nonempty before CR handling; larger inputs are outside this contract. LF is the only delimiter and a final unterminated segment is processed. Discard only segments whose length is already zero, then remove one trailing CR from each retained segment; therefore a segment containing only CR becomes an empty rejected record and counts toward the bound, while any other CR is data. A valid record is exactly <identifier><separator><priority>, with no quoting, escaping, or surrounding whitespace. An identifier is 1-16 ASCII characters: an uppercase A-Z first, then only uppercase A-Z, digits, or underscore. Priority is one or more ASCII digits, leading zeroes and zero are allowed, plus/minus signs, whitespace, non-ASCII digits, and values above Int32.MaxValue are rejected. Each valid record remains an independent entry, including duplicate identifiers; malformed records never remove valid entries.

The supplied constants are this candidate's fixed compile-time assignment; no alternate ordering or runtime selector is required. Sort using exactly this assigned algorithm: ordinal identifier ascending. The phrase is exhaustive: `priority descending then ordinal identifier ascending` uses descending integer priority as the primary key and StringComparer.Ordinal identifier as its tie-breaker; `ordinal identifier ascending` uses only StringComparer.Ordinal identifier and priority never participates. Write UTF-8 stdout as exactly six lines: `domain=trail-checkpoint`, `rejection-cap=2`, `order=ordinal identifier ascending`, `ids=` followed by the ordered identifiers joined by commas with no spaces or escaping (or exactly `ids=` when none are accepted), `accepted=` followed by the valid-record count, and `rejected=` followed by the smaller of the malformed-record count and numeric cap 2. Terminate every line, including the sixth, with one LF (U+000A); emit no CR or other text. The 10,000-segment bound prevents count overflow.

title: trail-checkpoint ranked admission
